newsitem.title: USA: Roberds sees Q3 profitability, sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Roberds sees Q3 profitability, sales rise.

text.p: Roberds Inc said Tuesday it expects record sales of about $95 million for the third quarter ending September 30, fueled in part by its Cincinnati megastore, which opened over the July 4 weekend.

The company said it expects net earnings of $0.14 to $0.18 per share. This is a "substantial improvement over second quarter results but below current street estimates due to expenses associated with the Cincinnati market," the company said.

The company said the Cincinnati store opening caused additional operating expenses that hurt its third quarter, but also produced strong sales that the company expects to continue into the fourth quarter.

The operating expenses have been "stabilized," and the company said it expects "the momentum in sales and profitability that developed during the third quarter will continue into the fourth quarter" with the opening of a new store in Atlanta, Georgia.

Roberds, which sells home furnishings, appliances and furniture, said it reported sales of $301 million in 1995 and has announced plans to open a second store in Columbus next year. The company's new Atlanta store is scheduled to open in November.
The company reported a net loss of $719,000, or $0.12 per share, in its second quarter and a net loss of $0.16 per share for its first half.
"We are extremely pleased that Roberds will return to profitability in the third quarter of 1996," company Chief Executive Officer Kenneth Fletcher stated.
